_provenance: Hand-derived qualitative sanity bounds, NOT digitized TouchSim/Saal et al. (2017) figure data and NOT recorded TouchSim output. See tests/fixtures/reference/README.md for exactly why and what was and was not obtainable in this environment.
citations: Johnson, K.O. (2001). The roles and functions of cutaneous mechanoreceptors. Current Opinion in Neurobiology 11:455-461.
Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science, 5th ed., Ch. 21.

Saal, H.P., Delhaye, B.P., Rayhaun, B.C., Bensmaia, S.J. (2017). Simulating tactile signals from the whole hand with millisecond precision. PNAS 114(28):E5693-E5702. Abstract and Fig. 1 describe RA1 afferents as responding only to indentation onset/offset and being silent during static hold, and SA1 afferents as sustaining a response through the hold phase -- the qualitative properties encoded below.

stimulus_protocol.description: Ramp-and-hold indentation: linear rise from 0 to peak amplitude over ramp_ms, held at peak for hold_ms, linear return to 0 over ramp_ms.

bounds.comment_sa: SA (slowly adapting) response late in the hold phase, divided by its peak response during the ramp, must stay above this fraction -- a sustained, roughly-proportional-to-depth response is the defining property of the SA class.
bounds.comment_ra: RA (rapidly adapting) response late in the hold phase, divided by its peak response at the ramp/onset transient, must fall below this fraction -- near-silence during a static hold is the defining property of the RA class.
